note: Rewritten from Sands' English revision of 1959; the original description is Haviland 1898 (Journal of the Linnean Society, Zoology 26: 358-442, as Termes hastatus). The present work adds alate measurements and the soldier head shape; soldier measurements lay outside the window read here and were not used.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Originally described as Termes hastatus Haviland, 1898 (Port Elizabeth, Cape Province, South Africa). In his revision Sands placed Hamitermes runconifer, atlanticus, capicola, gunni, kellyi, kenhardti, libertatis, londonensis, murraysburgi, schoombiensis and zuurbergi among its synonyms. Alate with antennae 14 or 15-segmented, the size variation wider than in the original description.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Additions to Haviland's original description: the antennae may be 14 or 15-segmented; the known size variation is wider. Measurements: head width (including compound eyes) 0.95—1.16, greatest diameter of the compound eye 0.23—0.29, ocellus length 0.07—0.10, width 0.10—0.14, ocellus–eye distance 0.03—0.08, pronotum width 0.76—1.04, length 0.44—0.64, hind tibia length 0.93—1.25, forewing length 8.00—12.6.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule longer than wide in dorsal view, from rounded-rectangular to broadly oval, narrowing anteriorly; in profile the upper surface flat, or slightly curved only between the fold above the fontanelle and the occiput and then evenly curved towards the occiput. Antennae 13—15-segmented.
